_comment: Function-semantics registry for derived-grain aggregate routing (spec section 6.2). DATA, not connector if-branches. Deliberately small in v1 (spec section 6.2: 'start with a deliberately small exact registry ... Breadth is added by theorem and known-answer tests, not by optimistic allow-listing'). Each entry declares the semantic function id, the sqlglot node/function aliases that canonicalise to it, input/output type signatures, volatility, totality, NULL behaviour, collation/timezone dependencies, exact source/target dialect profiles, and (later phases) derivation theorems. Unknown functions are SOURCE_ONLY by omission. No derivation theorems are enabled yet: capture + canonicalisation only.

timestamp_trunc._comment: sqlglot TimestampTrunc node (key 'timestamptrunc'). PostgreSQL DATE_TRUNC('month', ts) and BigQuery TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(ts, MONTH) both parse to this node. It truncates a TIMESTAMP. It is kept DISTINCT from date_trunc (the DATE-typed BigQuery DATE_TRUNC node) because the two are different typed operations with different input-type / timezone semantics (spec I5): the pre-binding fingerprint must NOT merge them. Any cross-node semantic equality is a later-phase registry theorem gated on the bound SemanticContext, never an accidental alias fold here.

date_trunc._comment: sqlglot DateTrunc node (key 'datetrunc'), e.g. BigQuery DATE_TRUNC(date_col, MONTH) over a DATE. Distinct from timestamp_trunc; truncates a DATE. Kept separate per spec I5 so a DATE truncation never fingerprint-collides with a TIMESTAMP truncation before binding.

try_cast._comment: TRY_CAST / SAFE_CAST returns NULL on invalid input rather than erroring. It has DIFFERENT null/error semantics from CAST (spec I5/I6), so it must NOT share CAST's identity — a folding of the two would let an errorable CAST fingerprint-match a NULL-returning TRY_CAST and change grouping/predicate behaviour.
